→ Self-custody before Aug 7
→ Skip non-urgent transfers Aug 7–12
→ 6–10 confirmations if you must send
→ Watch for exchange withdrawal pauses

tweets.author: axiomdesk.bsky.social
tweets.text:
Saylor (843,775 BTC) posted Aug 4: "Stand down."

Adam Back calls it fatally flawed.

Luke Dashjr, lead backer: "If BIP-110 fails, Bitcoin fails with it."

The wildcard? Foundry — 25–30% of global hashrate — quietly opened a miner vote. Result still unknown.

tweets.author: axiomdesk.bsky.social
tweets.text:
When block 961,632 arrives, every node running BIP-110 rules rejects normal Bitcoin blocks.

Those nodes fork onto a minority chain — a real bitcoin chain split.

And there's no replay protection. Any transaction you send could be valid on both chains at once.

tweets.author: axiomdesk.bsky.social
tweets.text:
🔴 The 2.7% Fork

BIP-110 wants to ban Ordinals, BRC-20, and Runes from Bitcoin.

It needs 55% miner support. Current signaling: 2.70%.

The mandatory signaling window opens at block 961,632 — Aug 7–9.

Why care about something almost certain to fail? 🧵

tweets.author: thebitcoinstrategy.bsky.social
tweets.text: The CBBI (Colin Talks Crypto's aggregate model) combines multiple on-chain signals into one number. Zero means cycle bottom. 100 means cycle top. It hit 94 when Bitcoin peaked near $120K. At 32, we are still in the middle, not the bottom.

tweets.author: thebitcoinstrategy.bsky.social
